source.title: Transformer Normalisation Layers and the Independence of Semantic Subspaces
source.authors: S. Menary; Samuel Kaski; André Freitas

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies interference between independent semantic subspaces caused by transformer normalization, not feature superposition under sparse co-activation or capacity pressure. Its reference to Toy Models of Superposition is background; it does not test the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own theory and experiments concern normalization-dependent semantic-subspace separability and simulated norm perturbations. These are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of the listed versions. Its cited discussion of feature superposition is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The paper studies interference between independent semantic subspaces caused by Pre-Norm normalisation and simulated norm noise in addition-task transformers. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only in related work and notes polysemanticity as a difficulty for interpretability. No result measures superposition, polysemantic neurons, SAE features or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Also: QKV-Norm matched Pre-Norm in-distribution (91.0% vs 91.4%) but generalised worse out-of-distribution (46.8% vs 66.7% extrapolation). The authors say they have not directly observed subspace interference.
record.recipe_differences: Not a reproduction of Toy Models of Superposition; the study develops a normalization-layer theory and evaluates trained addition-task transformers with simulated norm perturbations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported norm-spread bounds differ across model variations; collapse rates differ across Baseline, Alternate, and Large models. Sparse and non-sparse attention also show different stability under the tested perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: Theory: under Pre-Norm, independently attendable subspaces must be orthogonal constant-norm spheres; QKV-Norm needs only linear independence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalisation placement changes the geometric constraints for attention heads to separately read latent subspaces.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-Norm attention-weighted embedding norms lie within ±20% (90% coverage, Baseline; ~±30% in variants), wider for QKV-Norm; simulated norm noise degrades accuracy and triggers circuit collapse (1% at 11% noise Baseline; 7.5%/5.5% for Alternate/Large).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small Pre-Norm addition transformers, attended embeddings have narrow norm spread and sparse attention collapses to other tokens under ~5–11% norm noise.

record.problems: The authors state that they do not directly observe subspace independence or real-world interference. The interference is simulated with independent noise; the sparse-versus-non-sparse stability result may be confounded by relative importance and depth. Experiments use small models on a targeted addition task, and the authors call for evaluation on larger models and different corpora.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted task-performance comparisons between Pre-Norm and QKV-Norm, training-stability scans, and attention-sparsity comparisons because they do not measure the related subspace-interference findings recorded here. Per-layer figure curves were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: All: no toy model with sparse features exceeding dimensions, no overlap geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no capacity account of polysemantic neurons tested.
All: no analysis of causes of polysemanticity.
All: no measurement of feature spread across neurons or dictionary recovery.
All: semantic subspaces are multi-dimensional by definition, but the paper does not test whether superposed features are 1-D.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. Superposition appears only as a related-work citation, saying it stores more features than dimensions at the cost of interference. Polysemanticity is mentioned as a difficulty for interpretability. Neither is tested. All rows stay at versions ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: Sparse features outnumbering dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry of superposed features.
Capacity competition as an explanation of polysemantic neurons, including dedicated dimensions for important features.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Feature distribution across neurons or sparse features recovered from LLMs by dictionaries or SAEs.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Baseline Pre-Norm model
rows.stage_stated: trained on a base-10 integer-addition task
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention-weighted embedding L2-norm spread relative to the median, per head, excluding the begin-sequence token.
rows.note: The paper presents this as a bound on the representation effect in this model.

rows.stage_stated: trained on a base-10 integer-addition task
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention-weighted embedding L2-norm spread relative to the median, per head, excluding the begin-sequence token.
rows.value: Much wider spread than Pre-Norm; no numerical spread stated
rows.note: The text describes the QKV-Norm spread as wider; the figure gives no extractable numerical value.

rows.subject: Baseline Pre-Norm model
rows.stage_stated: trained on a base-10 integer-addition task
rows.operation_detail: Added uncorrelated uniform multiplicative noise to the L2 norms of q, k, and m in all layers during the forward pass.
rows.baseline: Unperturbed model; exact value for this noise experiment not stated
rows.note: This is an induced perturbation experiment, not a measurement of naturally occurring interference.
rows.check: Induced perturbation experiment (artificial noise on norms); measures accuracy degradation, not any superposition behaviour. Appendix C.2 adds Alternate model ≳20% drop, not recorded.

rows.stage_stated: trained on a base-10 integer-addition task
rows.operation_detail: Applied noise to q and k only for sparse-attention distributions.
rows.baseline: Unperturbed model; exact value not stated
rows.value: Stable under %-scale noise; exact accuracy values not stated
rows.note: The paper says sparse-attention distributions are stable in this regime.

rows.subject: Baseline Pre-Norm model
rows.stage_stated: trained on a base-10 integer-addition task
rows.operation_detail: Applied noise to q and k only for non-sparse-attention distributions.
rows.baseline: Unperturbed model; exact value not stated
rows.value: Non-sparse attention drives the accuracy drop at small noise levels
rows.note: The authors caution that this may reflect the relative importance of non-sparse distributions, rather than inherent stability differences alone.
